references.authors: Almeida FN, Leray C, Albignac M, et al.
references.title: Py-GC-MS/MS quantification of microplastics in vertebrate tissues: Addressing false positives of polyethylene
references.finding: Lipid interference causes polyethylene false positives in Py-GC/MS of tissue; markers with carbon chains longer than common lipids were needed to separate them.

references.authors: Bao W, Liu B, Rong S, et al.
references.title: Association Between Bisphenol A Exposure and Risk of All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality in US Adults
references.finding: Top vs bottom tertile of urinary BPA: all-cause mortality HR 1.49 (1.01-2.19), CVD mortality 1.46 (0.67-3.15), cancer mortality 0.98; 344 deaths.

references.authors: Beyer A, Schorgg P, Karavasiloglou N, et al.
references.title: Urinary phthalate concentrations and mortality risk: A population-based study
references.finding: Higher MBzP and MnBP (low-molecular-weight phthalate metabolites, not DEHP) were linked to higher mortality (top quartile HR 1.27 and 1.35).

references.authors: Blaauwendraad SM, Boxem AJ, Gaillard R, et al.
references.title: Periconception bisphenol and phthalate concentrations in women and men, time to pregnancy, and risk of miscarriage
references.n: 938 preconception and 1,366 pregnant women, 1,202 men (Generation R Next)
references.finding: Preconception BPS and a DINCH metabolite (mCOCH) in women were linked to longer time to pregnancy, but several phthalate metabolites were linked to shorter time to pregnancy; authors call results hypothesis-generating.

references.authors: Blakey A, Ott K, Peters T, et al.
references.title: Anti-PVC advocacy disguised as science (Response to Carlstedt et al., PVC flooring is related to human uptake of phthalates in infants)
references.finding: Letter titled 'Anti-PVC advocacy disguised as science' disputing the Carlstedt PVC-flooring study; a reply was published.

references.authors: Bornehag CG, Carlstedt F, Jönsson BA, et al.
references.title: Prenatal phthalate exposures and anogenital distance in Swedish boys
references.finding: First-trimester DiNP metabolites (the DEHP replacement) were associated with shorter anoscrotal distance, but the reduction was small (about 4% per IQR).

references.authors: Braun JM, Smith KW, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Variability of urinary phthalate metabolite and bisphenol A concentrations before and during pregnancy
references.finding: During pregnancy ICCs were 0.50 for MEP, 0.45 for MBP, 0.25 for MBzP, 0.12 for BPA and 0.08 for sum-DEHP; one spot sample adequately classified MEP and MBP but not DEHP or BPA.

references.authors: Buckley JP, Pacyga DC, Xun X, et al.
references.title: Gestational Exposure to 10 Classes of Priority Chemicals and Birth Outcomes in the ECHO Cohort
references.finding: Among 113 analytes in 10 chemical classes, several phthalates and alternative plasticizers were linked to slightly shorter gestation; summed DiNP metabolites: 0.6 days shorter, preterm birth OR 1.16 per IQR.

references.authors: Calafat AM, Needham LL, Silva MJ, et al.
references.title: Exposure to di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate among premature neonates in a neonatal intensive care unit
references.finding: Premature infants receiving intensive care via PVC devices had DEHP metabolite levels several-fold to orders of magnitude above the general population (geometric mean MEHP 100 vs 3.4 ng/mL).

references.authors: Camacho L, Lewis SM, Vanlandingham MM, et al.
references.title: A two-year toxicology study of bisphenol A (BPA) in Sprague-Dawley rats: CLARITY-BPA core study results
references.finding: Guideline-compliant 2-year CLARITY-BPA rat study (2.5-25,000 ug/kg/day): no BPA-related effects in in-life data; inconsistent lesions, with a possible relationship only at 25,000 ug/kg/day.

references.authors: Carlstedt F, Jönsson BA, Bornehag CG
references.title: PVC flooring is related to human uptake of phthalates in infants
references.finding: Infants with PVC flooring in the bedroom had significantly higher urinary MBzP (the BBzP metabolite).

references.authors: Carwile JL, Luu HT, Bassett LS, et al.
references.title: Polycarbonate bottle use and urinary bisphenol A concentrations
references.finding: A week of drinking cold beverages from polycarbonate bottles raised urinary BPA by 69%.

references.authors: Carwile JL, Ye X, Zhou X, et al.
references.title: Canned soup consumption and urinary bisphenol A: a randomized crossover trial
references.finding: One serving of canned soup a day for 5 days raised specific-gravity-adjusted urinary BPA to 20.8 ug/L vs 1.1 ug/L after fresh soup.

references.authors: Castellini C, Muselli M, Parisi A, et al.
references.title: Association between urinary bisphenol A concentrations and semen quality: A meta-analytic study
references.finding: Urinary BPA was only weakly associated with lower sperm motility, and the association disappeared after correction for publication bias; authors judge the link clinically negligible, if any.

references.authors: Charifson M, Seok E, Wang Y, et al.
references.title: Evaluating associations of bisphenol and phthalate exposure with time to pregnancy and subfecundity in a New York City pregnancy cohort
references.finding: First-trimester total bisphenols and some phthalate groups were linked to longer retrospective time to pregnancy and higher odds of subfecundity.

references.authors: Chavarro JE, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Chiu YH, et al.
references.title: Soy Intake Modifies the Relation Between Urinary Bisphenol A Concentrations and Pregnancy Outcomes Among Women Undergoing Assisted Reproduction
references.finding: Soy intake modified the BPA association: among women eating no soy, live birth fell from 54% to 17% across BPA quartiles; no association among soy consumers.

references.authors: Cox KD, Covernton GA, Davies HL, et al.
references.title: Human Consumption of Microplastics
references.finding: Estimated annual microplastic consumption of 39,000-52,000 particles, rising to 74,000-121,000 with inhalation.

references.authors: Cui C, Guo Z, Liu Y, et al.
references.title: Tissue-specific distribution of microplastics in human blood and carotid plaques: A paired sample analysis
references.finding: Paired blood and plaque Py-GC/MS found mean 75 ug/g in blood and 433 ug/g in plaque with only moderate correlation between them (r 0.30).

references.authors: den Braver-Sewradj SP, van Spronsen R, Hessel EVS
references.title: Substitution of bisphenol A: a review of the carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, and endocrine disruption potential of alternative substances
references.finding: Data for BPS, BPAF and to a lesser extent BPF indicate a reproductive-toxicity hazard with a possible endocrine mode of action; most other BPA alternatives have data gaps.

references.authors: Dewalque L, Pirard C, Vandepaer S, et al.
references.title: Temporal variability of urinary concentrations of phthalate metabolites, parabens and benzophenone-3 in a Belgian adult population
references.n: 32 Belgian adults, 11 urine spots over 4 months
references.finding: Within-person reproducibility was fair for MEP and MiBP (ICC 0.55-0.68) but lower for MBzP, MnBP and DEHP metabolites (ICC 0.20-0.49).

references.authors: Dhar S, Tomar A, N A, et al.
references.title: Phthalates as the silent saboteurs of male fertility via changes in semen quality: a systematic review
references.finding: Systematic review without meta-analysis: MEHP, DEHP and DBP associated with lower sperm concentration and morphology; certainty of evidence low to moderate because studies are observational and heterogeneous.

references.authors: Dodge LE, Williams PL, Williams MA, et al.
references.title: Associations between paternal urinary phthalate metabolite concentrations and reproductive outcomes among couples seeking fertility treatment
references.finding: Paternal MCPP and MCOP were associated with lower implantation and IVF live birth, but most paternal phthalate metabolites were not associated with outcomes.

references.authors: Due I, Rubio L, Catalán J, et al.
references.title: Mammalian reproductive and developmental toxicity of micro- and nanoplastics: a critical appraisal of evidence using the SciRAP tool
references.finding: SciRAP appraisal: of mammalian reproductive/developmental micro/nanoplastic studies only 7 were strong for risk assessment; particle characterization, dose and dose-response were often missing.

references.authors: Duty SM, Singh NP, Silva MJ, et al.
references.title: The relationship between environmental exposures to phthalates and DNA damage in human sperm using the neutral comet assay
references.finding: An IQR rise in MEP was associated with 3.6 um greater Comet extent in sperm; other metabolites were not clearly associated.

references.authors: Duty SM, Ackerman RM, Calafat AM, et al.
references.title: Personal care product use predicts urinary concentrations of some phthalate monoesters
references.finding: Men who used cologne or aftershave in the previous 48 h had about double urinary MEP (265 vs 108 ng/mL); each additional personal-care product raised MEP by 33%.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Contact Materials, Enzymes and Processing Aids (CEP), Silano V, Barat Baviera JM, et al.
references.title: Update of the risk assessment of di-butylphthalate (DBP), butyl-benzyl-phthalate (BBP), bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP), di-isononylphthalate (DINP) and di-isodecylphthalate (DIDP) for use in food contact materials
references.finding: EFSA set a group TDI of 50 ug/kg bw/day (as DEHP equivalents) for DBP, BBP, DEHP and DINP based on reduced fetal testosterone; aggregated dietary exposure was 0.9-7.2 (mean) to 1.6-11.7 (high) ug/kg/day, up to 23% of the group TDI; assessment called temporary.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Contact Materials, Enzymes and Processing Aids (CEP), Lambré C, Barat Baviera JM, et al.
references.title: Re-evaluation of the risks to public health related to the presence of bisphenol A (BPA) in foodstuffs
references.finding: EFSA lowered the BPA tolerable daily intake from 4 ug/kg to 0.2 ng/kg body weight per day (20,000-fold) based on Th17 immune effects in mice and concluded average and high dietary exposure exceed it by two to three orders of magnitude.

references.authors: Ehrlich S, Williams PL, Missmer SA, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol A concentrations and implantation failure among women undergoing in vitro fertilization
references.finding: Implantation failure odds rose across BPA quartiles (top quartile OR 2.11, 0.84-5.31; p-trend 0.06).

references.authors: Ehrlich S, Calafat AM, Humblet O, et al.
references.title: Handling of thermal receipts as a source of exposure to bisphenol A
references.finding: Handling thermal receipts for 2 h without gloves raised urinary BPA from 1.8 to 5.8 ug/L, peaking at 8-12 h; nitrile gloves prevented a significant rise.

references.authors: European Commission
references.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/3190 of 19 December 2024 on the use of bisphenol A (BPA) and other bisphenols and bisphenol derivatives in materials and articles intended to come into contact with food
references.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
references.finding: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/3190 bans BPA and its salts in food contact materials (plastics, coatings, varnishes, inks, adhesives, rubbers), with an 18-month transition to 20 July 2026 for most single-use items and 36 months (to 20 January 2028) for some uses; other hazardous bisphenols need authorization.

references.authors: Faber WD, Deyo JA, Stump DG, et al.
references.title: Developmental toxicity and uterotrophic studies with di-2-ethylhexyl terephthalate
references.journal: Birth Defects Res B Dev Reprod Toxicol
references.finding: Guideline developmental toxicity studies of DEHTP in rats (up to 747 mg/kg/day) and mice found no malformations or effects on implantation or fetal weight, and no estrogenic activity in a uterotrophic assay.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, Cantonwine DE, Rivera-González LO, et al.
references.title: Urinary phthalate metabolite associations with biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress across pregnancy in Puerto Rico
references.n: 54 women (oxidative stress) / 120 women (inflammation), PROTECT Puerto Rico
references.finding: Across repeated pregnancy samples, all phthalate metabolites were associated with higher urinary 8-isoprostane and 8-OHdG; IQR rises in MBP and MiBP went with about 49-50% higher 8-isoprostane.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, McElrath TF, Chen YH, et al.
references.title: Urinary phthalate metabolites and biomarkers of oxidative stress in pregnant women: a repeated measures analysis
references.n: 482 pregnant women (130 preterm cases, 352 controls; LIFECODES)
references.finding: Interquartile rises in urinary phthalate metabolites were associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane across up to four samples per woman, more strongly for MBzP, MBP and MiBP than DEHP metabolites.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, Cantonwine DE, McElrath TF, et al.
references.title: Repeated measures analysis of associations between urinary bisphenol-A concentrations and biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress in pregnancy
references.finding: An interquartile rise in urinary BPA was associated with 5-9% higher 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane and 9% higher plasma IL-6 across repeated pregnancy samples.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, Chen YH, VanderWeele TJ, et al.
references.title: Mediation of the Relationship between Maternal Phthalate Exposure and Preterm Birth by Oxidative Stress with Repeated Measurements across Pregnancy
references.n: 482 pregnant women (130 preterm cases, 352 controls; LIFECODES)
references.finding: Counterfactual mediation analysis: 8-isoprostane mediated an estimated 47-60% of the association between the DEHP metabolite MECPP and preterm birth (total OR 1.48-1.67).

references.authors: Fisher M, Arbuckle TE, Mallick R, et al.
references.title: Bisphenol A and phthalate metabolite urinary concentrations: Daily and across pregnancy variability
references.finding: BPA and all phthalate metabolites showed low reproducibility across pregnancy but much higher within a day; multiple samples across pregnancy are needed.

references.authors: Foster PM
references.title: Disruption of reproductive development in male rat offspring following in utero exposure to phthalate esters
references.finding: Review of rat studies: in-utero DBP, DEHP and BBP lower fetal testicular testosterone and INSL3, causing the 'phthalate syndrome' of hypospadias, cryptorchidism, malformed accessory glands, retained nipples and shorter anogenital distance.

references.authors: Friedman A, Welch BM, Keil AP, et al.
references.title: Periods of susceptibility for associations between phthalate exposure and preterm birth: Results from a pooled analysis of 16 US cohorts
references.finding: In the same pooled data, DEHP-metabolite associations with preterm birth were strongest for first- and second-trimester exposure (MEHP OR 1.15 and 1.11 per IQR) and null in the third trimester.

references.authors: Galloway TS, Baglin N, Lee BP, et al.
references.title: An engaged research study to assess the effect of a 'real-world' dietary intervention on urinary bisphenol A (BPA) levels in teenagers
references.finding: A self-designed 7-day diet to avoid BPA did not lower urinary BPA overall (p=0.25); participants found BPA-free food hard to identify and unlikely to sustain.

references.authors: Génard-Walton M, Warembourg C, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Using mixture and exposome methods to assess the associations and interactions of chemical biomarkers with semen parameters
references.finding: Across four mixture/exposome models of 24 biomarkers (BPA, parabens, triclosan, 17 phthalate metabolites, hair mercury), the consistent signals were mercury (positive) and triclosan (negative); the overall mixture had small, imprecise associations with semen parameters.

references.authors: Gerofke A, Lange R, Vogel N, et al.
references.title: Phthalates and substitute plasticizers: Main achievements from the European human biomonitoring initiative HBM4EU
references.finding: Health-based biomonitoring guidance values were exceeded in up to 5% of participants; for about 17% of children and teens, a mixture risk from five reprotoxic phthalates could not be excluded; food and personal-care products were main sources.

references.authors: Ghayda RA, Williams PL, Chavarro JE, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol S concentrations: Potential predictors of and associations with semen quality parameters among men attending a fertility center
references.finding: Men with detectable BPS had lower sperm concentration (30.7 vs 38.3 million/mL) and semen volume, mostly among overweight men; BPS tracked fabric softener, paint and recent beef and cheese intake.

references.authors: Goldstone AE, Chen Z, Perry MJ, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol A and semen quality, the LIFE Study
references.finding: In a general-population preconception cohort, urinary BPA was not associated with 34 of 35 semen measures; the only significant finding was less sperm DNA fragmentation with higher BPA.

references.authors: Gougeon A
references.title: Dynamics of follicular growth in the human: a model from preliminary results
references.finding: The human ovulatory follicle begins its final growth about 85 days before ovulation; the dominant follicle is recruited 15-20 days before ovulation.

references.authors: Guo Y, Rong M, Fan Y, et al.
references.title: The Presence of Microplastics in Human Semen and Their Associations with Semen Quality
references.finding: Microplastics (LD-IR) were found in 34 of 45 semen samples; men with PET particles had lower progressive motility (20.6 vs 34.9%, p=0.056); no link with concentration or count.

references.authors: Hagobian T, Smouse A, Streeter M, et al.
references.title: Randomized Intervention Trial to Decrease Bisphenol A Urine Concentrations in Women: Pilot Study
references.finding: A 3-week intervention (BPA-free products, glass containers, weekly counselling) lowered creatinine-adjusted urinary BPA vs control (treatment x time p=0.04).

references.authors: Harley KG, Kogut K, Madrigal DS, et al.
references.title: Reducing Phthalate, Paraben, and Phenol Exposure from Personal Care Products in Adolescent Girls: Findings from the HERMOSA Intervention Study
references.finding: Three days of personal-care products free of phthalates, parabens, triclosan and BP-3 lowered urinary MEP by 27% and methyl/propyl paraben by about 44-45%; MnBP and MiBP did not change.

references.authors: Harray AJ, Lucas AD, Herrmann SE, et al.
references.title: Low-plastic diet and urinary levels of plastic-associated phthalates and bisphenols: the randomized controlled PERTH Trial
references.finding: A 7-day diet of food sourced to minimize plastic contact, with plastic-free kitchenware and personal-care products, cut urinary MnBP by 37.5%, MBzP by 53.5% and BPA by 59.7% vs no intervention; personal-care swaps alone lowered MnBP; Minderoo-funded.

references.authors: Hauser R, Duty S, Godfrey-Bailey L, et al.
references.title: Medications as a source of human exposure to phthalates
references.finding: A man taking enteric-coated mesalamine (Asacol) had urinary MBP of 16,868 ng/mL, more than two orders of magnitude above the NHANES 95th percentile.

references.authors: Hauser R, Meeker JD, Duty S, et al.
references.title: Altered semen quality in relation to urinary concentrations of phthalate monoester and oxidative metabolites
references.finding: Dose-response links of MBP with low sperm concentration (OR 3.3 top quartile) and motility; suggestive links for MBzP; single spot urine.

references.authors: Hauser R, Meeker JD, Singh NP, et al.
references.title: DNA damage in human sperm is related to urinary levels of phthalate monoester and oxidative metabolites
references.finding: MEP was associated with more neutral-Comet sperm DNA damage; MEHP was associated only after adjusting for the oxidative metabolite MEHHP (Comet extent +17.3%, tail % +17.5% per IQR).

references.authors: Hauser R, Gaskins AJ, Souter I, et al.
references.title: Urinary Phthalate Metabolite Concentrations and Reproductive Outcomes among Women Undergoing in Vitro Fertilization: Results from the EARTH Study
references.finding: Women in the top vs bottom quartile of urinary DEHP metabolites had fewer and fewer mature oocytes and 19 percentage points lower clinical pregnancy and live birth per cycle.

references.authors: Heindel JJ, Belcher S, Flaws JA, et al.
references.title: Data integration, analysis, and interpretation of eight academic CLARITY-BPA studies
references.finding: Integration of eight academic CLARITY-BPA studies on the same animals: developmental BPA affected brain, prostate, urinary tract, ovary, mammary gland and heart, often at the lowest dose (2.5 ug/kg/day) and non-monotonically.

references.authors: HELLER CG, CLERMONT Y
references.title: Spermatogenesis in man: an estimate of its duration
references.finding: One cycle of the human seminiferous epithelium lasts about 16 days and complete spermatogenesis about 64 days.

references.authors: Hernandez LM, Xu EG, Larsson HCE, et al.
references.title: Plastic Teabags Release Billions of Microparticles and Nanoparticles into Tea
references.finding: Steeping one plastic teabag at 95 C released about 11.6 billion microplastic and 3.1 billion nanoplastic particles into a cup.

references.authors: Hernández-Díaz S, Mitchell AA, Kelley KE, et al.
references.title: Medications as a potential source of exposure to phthalates in the U.S. population
references.finding: Users of mesalamine formulations that may contain DBP had mean urinary MBP 50 times higher than non-users (2,257 vs 46 ug/L); some didanosine, omeprazole and theophylline products were linked to higher MEP.

references.authors: Hormann AM, Vom Saal FS, Nagel SC, et al.
references.title: Holding thermal receipt paper and eating food after using hand sanitizer results in high serum bioactive and urine total levels of bisphenol A (BPA)
references.finding: Holding thermal receipt paper right after using a hand sanitizer with penetration enhancers, then eating fries by hand, raised serum unconjugated BPA to about 7 ng/mL within 90 min.

references.authors: Hu CJ, Garcia MA, Nihart A, et al.
references.title: Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis
references.finding: Py-GC/MS found microplastics in every testis (mean 328 ug/g in humans, mostly polyethylene), with polymer-specific negative correlations with sperm count in dogs.

references.authors: Hu CJ, Garcia MA, Nihart A, et al.
references.title: Response to comment on: "Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis"
references.finding: Authors' response to the comment on the testis microplastics study.

references.authors: Hunt PA, Koehler KE, Susiarjo M, et al.
references.title: Bisphenol a exposure causes meiotic aneuploidy in the female mouse
references.finding: Accidental and then deliberate low-dose BPA exposure during the final stages of oocyte growth caused dose-dependent meiotic aneuploidy in female mice.

references.authors: Hussain KA, Romanova S, Okur I, et al.
references.title: Assessing the Release of Microplastics and Nanoplastics from Plastic Containers and Reusable Food Pouches: Implications for Human Health
references.finding: Microwaving some plastic containers released up to 4.22 million microplastic and 2.11 billion nanoplastic particles per cm2 of plastic in 3 minutes.

references.authors: Hutter HP, Kundi M, Hohenblum P, et al.
references.title: Life without plastic: A family experiment and biomonitoring study
references.finding: After a family removed plastics from their home, urinary BPA was below quantification, but over two further months phthalate metabolites fell in some members and rose in the mother.

references.authors: Hyman S, Acevedo J, Giannarelli C, et al.
references.title: Phthalate exposure from plastics and cardiovascular disease: global estimates of attributable mortality and years life lost
references.finding: Burden model applying a US hazard ratio to regional DEHP exposure estimates: 356,238 cardiovascular deaths in 2018 (13.5% of CVD deaths at ages 55-64) attributed to DEHP; funded by Bloomberg Philanthropies, Beyond Petrochemicals and NIH.

references.authors: Hyman S, Acevedo J, Trasande L
references.title: Preterm birth attributable to exposure to chemicals used in plastic materials: a global estimate
references.finding: Burden model applying a hazard ratio from a previous cohort to global exposure estimates: 1.97 million preterm births in 2018 (8.7% of the global total) attributed to DEHP.

references.authors: Ilki FY
references.title: Increased seminal microplastic burden in men with varicocele: a controlled clinical study
references.finding: Light-microscopy counts found more seminal microplastics in varicocele (median 8 vs 4 particles/mL); microplastic load correlated with lower concentration, motility and morphology.

references.authors: Jensen TK, Frederiksen H, Kyhl HB, et al.
references.title: Prenatal Exposure to Phthalates and Anogenital Distance in Male Infants from a Low-Exposed Danish Cohort (2010-2012)
references.finding: In a low-exposed cohort, no consistent associations were seen between any third-trimester phthalate metabolite and anogenital distance or penile width at 3 months.

references.authors: Jiang Y, Xu Y, Xiao S, et al.
references.title: Phthalate and DINCH exposure and ovarian reserve markers among women seeking infertility care
references.finding: Most conventional phthalate metabolites were inversely associated with antral follicle count, DINCH metabolites with higher FSH; the phthalate+DINCH mixture went with 8.6% lower AFC.

references.authors: Johns LE, Cooper GS, Galizia A, et al.
references.title: Exposure assessment issues in epidemiology studies of phthalates
references.finding: Phthalate metabolite half-lives are 3-18 h; intraclass correlations of repeated urine samples are about 0.3-0.6 for DEP, DBP, DiBP and BBzP metabolites and 0.1-0.3 for DEHP, DiNP and DiDP; US and German exposures to DEP, BBzP, DBP and DEHP declined after 2001.

references.authors: Kiwitt-Cárdenas J, Adoamnei E, Arense-Gonzalo JJ, et al.
references.title: Associations between urinary concentrations of bisphenol A and sperm DNA fragmentation in young men
references.finding: No association between urinary BPA and sperm DNA fragmentation overall; a positive association only in the subgroup with SDF above 30%.

references.authors: Knox KE, Schwarzman MR, Rudel RA, et al.
references.title: Trends in NHANES Biomonitored Exposures in California and the United States following Enactment of California's Proposition 65
references.finding: Median BPA fell 15% after California's Prop 65 listing while unlisted BPS rose 20% over the same period, suggesting substitution.

references.authors: Koch HM, Bolt HM, Angerer J
references.title: Di(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP) metabolites in human urine and serum after a single oral dose of deuterium-labelled DEHP
references.finding: After a labelled DEHP dose, urinary metabolites peaked at 2-4 h; first-phase excretion half-lives were about 2 h and second-phase 5-10 h.

references.authors: Kong F, Fang L, Gui Y, et al.
references.title: Polyethylene and Polyvinyl Chloride Nanoplastics in Human Follicular Fluid and Seminal Plasma: Impact on Fertilization and Sperm Quality
references.finding: Py-GC/MS found polyethylene and PVC nanoplastics in follicular fluid and seminal plasma; higher follicular PE/PVC tertiles had lower fertilization rates and seminal PVC tracked lower motility, but neither was linked to implantation or pregnancy.

references.authors: Kortenkamp A, Martin O, Iacovidou E, et al.
references.title: Drivers of divergent assessments of bisphenol-A hazards to semen quality by various European agencies, regulators and scientists
references.finding: Analysis of why EFSA and the German BfR diverge: BfR proposed an alternative TDI 1,000-fold higher than EFSA's, based on adult sperm-count effects, and rejected the immunotoxicity endpoint; both agencies discounted gestational-exposure studies.

references.authors: Lane T, de Ruijter VN, Wardani I, et al.
references.title: A QA/QC screening framework to assess studies reporting microplastic presence in human organs, tissues, and bodily fluids
references.finding: QA/QC screen of human-tissue microplastic studies: none met all essential criteria; common gaps in sample representativeness, positive controls and blank documentation.

references.authors: Lange R, Apel P, Rousselle C, et al.
references.title: The European Human Biomonitoring Initiative (HBM4EU): Human biomonitoring guidance values for selected phthalates and a substitute plasticizer
references.finding: HBM4EU human-biomonitoring guidance values for adults, e.g. 0.5 mg/L urine for the sum of 5-oxo- and 5-OH-MEHP, 0.19 mg/L MnBP, 3 mg/L MBzP, 4.5 mg/L for DINCH metabolites.

references.authors: Lehmler HJ, Liu B, Gadogbe M, et al.
references.title: Exposure to Bisphenol A, Bisphenol F, and Bisphenol S in U.S. Adults and Children: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013-2014
references.finding: BPA, BPS and BPF were detected in 95.7%, 89.4% and 66.5% of urine samples; median adult BPA 1.24 ug/L vs 0.35-0.37 ug/L for BPF and BPS.

references.authors: Lessmann F, Schütze A, Weiss T, et al.
references.title: Metabolism and urinary excretion kinetics of di(2-ethylhexyl) terephthalate (DEHTP) in three male volunteers after oral dosage
references.finding: After an oral DEHTP dose about 16% was recovered as specific metabolites, 95% of it within the first 24 h; 5cx-MEPTP was the main biomarker.

references.authors: Lessmann F, Kolossa-Gehring M, Apel P, et al.
references.title: German Environmental Specimen Bank: 24-hour urine samples from 1999 to 2017 reveal rapid increase in exposure to the para-phthalate plasticizer di(2-ethylhexyl) terephthalate (DEHTP)
references.finding: The DEHP substitute DEHTP went from under 10% detection before 2009 to 100% in 2017 (median 3.35 ug/L metabolite), still far below German guidance values (median intake 0.74 ug/kg/day vs TDI 1,000).

references.authors: Li DK, Zhou Z, Miao M, et al.
references.title: Urine bisphenol-A (BPA) level in relation to semen quality
references.n: 218 men with and without occupational BPA exposure (China)
references.finding: Men with detectable urinary BPA had more than three times the risk of low sperm concentration and vitality and more than four times the risk of low count; associations persisted at environmental levels.

references.authors: Liu C, Duan P, Chen YJ, et al.
references.title: Mediation of the relationship between phthalate exposure and semen quality by oxidative stress among 1034 reproductive-aged Chinese men
references.finding: Every phthalate metabolite rose with urinary 8-OHdG, 8-isoPGF2a and HNE-MA; 8-isoPGF2a suggestively mediated 12% of the MBP-sperm concentration link and 8-OHdG 32% of the MEP-morphology link (p<0.10).

references.authors: Lü L, Liu Y, Yang Y, et al.
references.title: Bisphenol A Exposure Interferes with Reproductive Hormones and Decreases Sperm Counts: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiological Studies
references.finding: Urinary BPA was associated with slightly lower sperm concentration and total count and with higher SHBG and estradiol, but not robustly with below-reference semen quality.

references.authors: Machtinger R, Combelles CM, Missmer SA, et al.
references.title: Bisphenol-A and human oocyte maturation in vitro
references.finding: Sibling human oocytes cultured with BPA (20 ng/mL to 20 ug/mL) showed dose-dependent falls in maturation to metaphase II and more abnormal spindles and chromosome misalignment.

references.authors: Machtinger R, Gaskins AJ, Racowsky C, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of biomarkers of phthalates and phthalate alternatives and IVF outcomes
references.finding: Higher DEHP metabolites were linked to fewer total, mature and fertilized oocytes and top-quality embryos, but no phthalate metabolite was linked to implantation, clinical pregnancy or live birth; DINCH metabolites showed no associations.

references.authors: Majdi L, Tizro G, Salehpour S, et al.
references.title: Association between Particulate Matter (PM₂.₅), Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂), Bisphenol A (BPA), and Phthalates and Infertility Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
references.finding: Pooled ART studies: BPA associated with lower AMH (SMD -0.42) and clinical pregnancy (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.81-0.85), phthalates with lower antral follicle count (SMD -0.38); no effect on time to pregnancy; heterogeneity 58-85%.

references.authors: Marfella R, Prattichizzo F, Sardu C, et al.
references.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas and Cardiovascular Events
references.finding: Patients with detectable micro/nanoplastics (mainly polyethylene, PVC) in carotid plaque had a higher risk of MI, stroke or death over 34 months (HR 4.53, 2.00-10.27).

references.authors: Marfella R, Prattichizzo F
references.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas. Reply
references.finding: Authors' reply to several NEJM letters questioning contamination control, confounding and measurement in the plaque-microplastics cohort.

references.authors: Martínez Steele E, Khandpur N, da Costa Louzada ML, et al.
references.title: Association between dietary contribution of ultra-processed foods and urinary concentrations of phthalates and bisphenol in a nationally representative sample of the US population aged 6 years and older
references.finding: Urinary DiNP, mCNP, mCPP, MBzP and BPF rose monotonically across quintiles of ultra-processed food intake.

references.authors: Meeker JD, Ehrlich S, Toth TL, et al.
references.title: Semen quality and sperm DNA damage in relation to urinary bisphenol A among men from an infertility clinic
references.finding: An IQR rise in urinary BPA was linked to 23% lower sperm concentration, 13% lower normal morphology and 10% more Comet tail DNA.

references.authors: Messerlian C, Wylie BJ, Mínguez-Alarcón L, et al.
references.title: Urinary Concentrations of Phthalate Metabolites and Pregnancy Loss Among Women Conceiving with Medically Assisted Reproduction
references.finding: Biochemical pregnancy loss rose across sum-DEHP quartiles (top quartile RR 3.4, 0.97-11.7; p-trend 0.04); other phthalates were not associated; estimates imprecise.

references.authors: Mhaouty-Kodja S, Zalko D, Tait S, et al.
references.title: A critical review to identify data gaps and improve risk assessment of bisphenol A alternatives for human health
references.finding: BPS and BPF are now found in people worldwide and are being regulated for toxicity; newer BPA alternatives have large toxicology data gaps (regrettable substitution).

references.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Gaskins AJ, Chiu YH, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol A concentrations and association with in vitro fertilization outcomes among women from a fertility clinic
references.finding: In the expanded Boston cohort, urinary BPA was not associated with peak estradiol, fertilization, embryo quality, implantation, clinical pregnancy or live birth.

references.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Bellavia A, Gaskins AJ, et al.
references.title: Paternal mixtures of urinary concentrations of phthalate metabolites, bisphenol A and parabens in relation to pregnancy outcomes among couples attending a fertility center
references.finding: A paternal DEHP-metabolite factor was linked to a higher probability of failing to reach live birth (HR 1.41 per IQR); the BPA/non-DEHP factor HR 1.24 (0.97-1.59) and parabens null.

references.authors: Mok-Lin E, Ehrlich S, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol A concentrations and ovarian response among women undergoing IVF
references.finding: Each log-unit increase in urinary BPA was associated with 12% fewer oocytes retrieved and 213 pg/mL lower peak estradiol.

references.authors: A Monikh F, Materić D, Valsami-Jones E, et al.
references.title: Challenges in studying microplastics in human brain
references.finding: Letter from analytical chemists setting out challenges in measuring microplastics in human brain, including Py-GC/MS interference.

references.authors: Nihart AJ, Garcia MA, El Hayek E, et al.
references.title: Bioaccumulation of microplastics in decedent human brains
references.n: decedent brain, liver and kidney samples
references.finding: Pyrolysis GC/MS, infrared and electron microscopy reported micro/nanoplastics, mainly polyethylene, in human liver, kidney and brain, with higher proportions of polyethylene in brain.

references.authors: Nihart AJ, Garcia MA, El Hayek E, et al.
references.title: Author Correction: Bioaccumulation of microplastics in decedent human brains
references.finding: Author correction to the decedent-brain microplastics paper.

references.authors: Oh J, Choi JW, Ahn YA, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of bisphenol S in humans after single oral administration
references.finding: Oral BPS was absorbed within about 1 h and excreted with a terminal half-life under 7 h (6.8 h).

references.authors: Oskar S, Mook J, Smith MK, et al.
references.title: Temporal trends in phthalate metabolite exposure of girls in the United States across sociodemographic factors and intersectional social identities: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2001-2018
references.finding: Low- and high-molecular-weight phthalate metabolites declined between 2001 and 2018, with persistent sociodemographic differences in low-molecular-weight phthalates.

references.authors: Pacchierotti F, Ranaldi R, Eichenlaub-Ritter U, et al.
references.title: Evaluation of aneugenic effects of bisphenol A in somatic and germ cells of the mouse
references.finding: Single, 7-day or 7-week oral BPA exposure did not induce hyperploidy or polyploidy in mouse oocytes or zygotes; only prematurely separated chromatids after chronic exposure, without effect on segregation.

references.authors: Peng CY, Tsai EM, Kao TH, et al.
references.title: Canned food intake and urinary bisphenol a concentrations: a randomized crossover intervention study
references.finding: A canned-food meal raised urinary BPA by up to 206% at 4 h, returning to baseline by 24 h.

references.authors: Peters AE, Ford EA, Roman SD, et al.
references.title: Impact of Bisphenol A and its alternatives on oocyte health: a scoping review
references.finding: Scoping review: nearly all in vitro and animal studies of BPA and its alternatives (BPS, BPF, BPAF and others) found adverse oocyte effects, often below 'safe' levels; 11 of 21 human observational studies linked higher urinary BPA to lower antral follicle count or oocyte yield.

references.authors: Plachetka L, Stanislas V, Bauer A, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol levels and blood pressure after soda consumption from cans, PET and glass bottles
references.finding: Soda from cans raised urinary BPA by 22% vs PET bottles; BPS, BPF and BPE appeared regardless of packaging.

references.authors: Potts C, Harbolic A, Murphy M, et al.
references.title: A common phthalate replacement disrupts ovarian function in young adult mice
references.finding: In young adult mice, 10 days of oral DEHTP (from 10 ug/kg) altered ovarian follicle counts and gene expression, and DEHTP/MEHTP slowed follicle growth in vitro.

references.authors: Prueitt RL, Goodman JE
references.title: WITHDRAWN: Letter to editor: Evidence evaluated by EFSA does not support lowering the temporary tolerable daily intake for bisphenol A
references.finding: RETRACTED/WITHDRAWN letter arguing EFSA's evidence did not support lowering the BPA TDI; withdrawn at the request of the author(s) and/or editor. Cited only to flag it.

references.authors: Qian N, Gao X, Lang X, et al.
references.title: Rapid single-particle chemical imaging of nanoplastics by SRS microscopy
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Single-particle SRS imaging estimated about 240,000 micro/nanoplastic particles per litre of bottled water, about 90% nanoplastics.

references.authors: Qu J, Zeng J, Mou L, et al.
references.title: Plastic tableware use, microplastic accumulation, and sperm quality: from epidemiological evidence to FOXA1/p38 mechanistic insights
references.finding: Microplastics were detected in 55.5% of semen samples; frequent plastic-tableware use tracked semen microplastics, and microplastics with lower concentration only in a subgroup (BMI <24, frequent use).

references.authors: Radke EG, Braun JM, Meeker JD, et al.
references.title: Phthalate exposure and male reproductive outcomes: A systematic review of the human epidemiological evidence
references.finding: EPA systematic review: robust evidence linking DEHP and DBP to male reproductive outcomes (AGD, semen, testosterone), moderate for DINP and BBP, slight for DIBP and DEP.

references.authors: Radke EG, Glenn BS, Braun JM, et al.
references.title: Phthalate exposure and female reproductive and developmental outcomes: a systematic review of the human epidemiological evidence
references.finding: EPA systematic review: moderate evidence linking DEHP, DBP and DEP to preterm birth; slight or indeterminate evidence for time to pregnancy, puberty and spontaneous abortion.

references.authors: Rauert C, Charlton N, Bagley A, et al.
references.title: Assessing the Efficacy of Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry for Nanoplastic and Microplastic Analysis in Human Blood
references.finding: Py-GC/MS polyethylene and PVC signals in blood suffer matrix false positives; realistic detection limits were up to 20 times higher than nominal and no polymer other than interfered PE exceeded them.

references.authors: Rochester JR, Bolden AL
references.title: Bisphenol S and F: A Systematic Review and Comparison of the Hormonal Activity of Bisphenol A Substitutes
references.finding: BPS and BPF have hormonal potency in the same order of magnitude as BPA (estrogenic, antiestrogenic, androgenic, antiandrogenic); authors employed by TEDX, an endocrine-disruption advocacy nonprofit.

references.authors: Rudel RA, Gray JM, Engel CL, et al.
references.title: Food packaging and bisphenol A and bis(2-ethyhexyl) phthalate exposure: findings from a dietary intervention
references.finding: Three days of fresh, unpackaged food cut urinary BPA by 66% and DEHP metabolites by 53-56% (geometric means).

references.authors: Sathyanarayana S, Alcedo G, Saelens BE, et al.
references.title: Unexpected results in a randomized dietary trial to reduce phthalate and bisphenol A exposures
references.finding: A 5-day catered 'low-exposure' diet unexpectedly raised urinary DEHP metabolites (to an estimated intake above EPA and EFSA limits for children) because ingredients such as ground coriander and milk were contaminated.

references.authors: Silva MJ, Wong LY, Samandar E, et al.
references.title: Exposure to di-2-ethylhexyl terephthalate in the U.S. general population from the 2015-2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
references.finding: DEHTP metabolites were detected in 96-99.9% of the US population; levels rose with household income and were higher in females and children.

references.authors: Stahlhut RW, Welshons WV, Swan SH
references.title: Bisphenol A data in NHANES suggest longer than expected half-life, substantial nonfood exposure, or both
references.finding: Urinary BPA barely fell with longer fasting (population-based half-life 43 h), suggesting substantial non-food exposure, storage, or both.

references.authors: Sturgeon SR, Flynn D, Kaiser AB, et al.
references.title: Urinary levels of phthalate metabolites and cardiovascular disease mortality (NHANES, 1999-2008)
references.finding: No urinary phthalate metabolite was associated with cardiovascular mortality (top vs bottom quartile HRs 0.73-1.4, all non-significant; 175 CVD deaths).

references.authors: Swan SH, Main KM, Liu F, et al.
references.title: Decrease in anogenital distance among male infants with prenatal phthalate exposure
references.finding: Prenatal MBP, MEP, MBzP and MiBP were inversely related to boys' anogenital index; top vs bottom MBP quartile OR 10.2 for shorter-than-expected AGI.

references.authors: Swan SH, Sathyanarayana S, Barrett ES, et al.
references.title: First trimester phthalate exposure and anogenital distance in newborns
references.finding: First-trimester DEHP metabolites were inversely associated with both anogenital distance measures in boys but not girls; no other phthalate was associated; single urine sample and between-centre differences were limitations.

references.authors: Symeonides C, Aromataris E, Mulders Y, et al.
references.title: An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses Evaluating Associations between Human Health and Exposure to Major Classes of Plastic-Associated Chemicals
references.finding: Umbrella review of 52 systematic reviews: phthalates linked to pregnancy loss, reduced sperm quality and insulin resistance, BPA to PCOS, type 2 diabetes and CVD; most reviews of moderate quality; partly funded by the Minderoo Foundation.

references.authors: Teeguarden JG, Calafat AM, Ye X, et al.
references.title: Twenty-four hour human urine and serum profiles of bisphenol a during high-dietary exposure
references.finding: During three high-BPA meals, urinary total BPA peaked about 2.75 h after a meal; serum BPA was detectable only at exposures well above the US 95th percentile.

references.authors: Thayer KA, Doerge DR, Hunt D, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of bisphenol A in humans following a single oral administration
references.finding: After an oral dose of deuterated BPA, unconjugated BPA peaked at 1.3 h and the terminal half-life of total and unconjugated BPA was about 6.2-6.4 h.

references.authors: Trasande L, Liu B, Bao W
references.title: Phthalates and attributable mortality: A population-based longitudinal cohort study and cost analysis
references.finding: High-molecular-weight and DEHP metabolites were linked to higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.14 and 1.10 per unit; top tertile 1.48 and 1.42); extrapolation gave 90,761-107,283 attributable deaths a year among Americans aged 55-64, assuming causality.

references.authors: Vernet C, Philippat C, Agier L, et al.
references.title: An Empirical Validation of the Within-subject Biospecimens Pooling Approach to Minimize Exposure Misclassification in Biomarker-based Studies
references.n: 16 pregnant women (all voids, several weeks) plus simulation
references.finding: One spot urine sample produced 69% attenuation bias in a BPA dose-response; about 18 samples were needed to bring bias down to 10%.

references.authors: Vom Saal FS, Antoniou M, Belcher SM, et al.
references.title: The Conflict between Regulatory Agencies over the 20,000-Fold Lowering of the Tolerable Daily Intake (TDI) for Bisphenol A (BPA) by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA)
references.finding: Commentary endorsing EFSA's TDI and criticizing the German BfR and US FDA for relying on industry-funded guideline studies and rejecting academic findings.

references.authors: Wang Q, Chi F, Liu Y, et al.
references.title: Polyethylene microplastic exposure adversely affects oocyte quality in human and mouse
references.finding: Polyethylene was the most common microplastic in follicular fluid (86%) and correlated with lower fertilization rate (r -0.41); PE-exposed mice had fewer and poorer-quality oocytes and more ROS.

references.authors: Wang H, He H, Wei Y, et al.
references.title: Do phthalates and their metabolites cause poor semen quality? A systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological studies on risk of decline in sperm quality
references.finding: Urinary MBP (pooled OR 2.19) and MBzP (OR 1.88) and semen DEHP (r -0.23) were associated with low sperm concentration; no significant links with motility or morphology or for MEP and other metabolites.

references.authors: Wehrli L, Martin OV, Trasande L, et al.
references.title: Reproductive toxicity of micro- and nanoplastics: Insights from experimental and human studies
references.finding: Scoping review: micro/nanoplastics found in reproductive tissues and fluids; 30 animal studies report altered semen, folliculogenesis or litter size; particle vs additive effects cannot be separated.

references.authors: Welch BM, Keil AP, Buckley JP, et al.
references.title: Associations Between Prenatal Urinary Biomarkers of Phthalate Exposure and Preterm Birth: A Pooled Study of 16 US Cohorts
references.finding: Each interquartile-range rise in urinary MBP, MiBP, MECPP or MCPP across pregnancy was linked to 12-16% higher odds of preterm birth; modelled 30% and 50% cuts in the phthalate mixture would prevent about 6 and 11 preterm births per 1,000 live births.

references.authors: Wittassek M, Angerer J
references.title: Phthalates: metabolism and exposure
references.finding: At least 74% of an oral DEHP dose and 44% of DiNP are excreted in urine; median daily intakes in Germany were 2.7 ug/kg DEHP, 2.1 DnBP, 1.5 DiBP, 0.6 DiNP; children had higher exposure.

references.authors: Yang TC, Jovanovic N, Chong F, et al.
references.title: Interventions to Reduce Exposure to Synthetic Phenols and Phthalates from Dietary Intake and Personal Care Products: a Scoping Review
references.finding: Scoping review: interventions that removed sources generally lowered phenol and phthalate biomarkers within days, but compliance and contamination limited success, and policy may matter more than individual behaviour.

references.authors: Yang Y, Zhang F, Jiang Z, et al.
references.title: Microplastics are associated with elevated atherosclerotic risk and increased vascular complexity in acute coronary syndrome patients
references.finding: Blood microplastics (Py-GC/MS) were higher in acute coronary syndrome than controls and tracked IL-6 and IL-12p70; cross-sectional.

references.authors: Ye X, Wong LY, Bishop AM, et al.
references.title: Variability of urinary concentrations of bisphenol A in spot samples, first morning voids, and 24-hour collections
references.n: 8 adults collecting every void for a week
references.finding: For spot samples, 70% of BPA variance was within a day, outweighing between-person variance (9%).

references.authors: Yland JJ, Zhang Y, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Phthalate and DINCH urinary concentrations across pregnancy and risk of preterm birth
references.finding: Mean pregnancy sum-DEHP was imprecisely linked to preterm birth (RR 1.21, 0.84-1.72 per ln unit), with the clearest signal in the third trimester (RR 1.51); detection of a DINCH metabolite also appeared positively related to preterm birth.

references.authors: Yuan M, Chai J, Song J, et al.
references.title: Association of bisphenol A exposure with in vitro fertilization outcomes: A meta-analysis and systematic review
references.finding: Higher BPA was associated with lower normal fertilization rates and fewer high-quality embryos in IVF/ICSI, but not with clinical pregnancy, blastocyst formation or implantation.

references.authors: Zhang C, Zhang G, Sun K, et al.
references.title: Association of mixed exposure to microplastics with sperm dysfunction: a multi-site study in China
references.finding: Raman microscopy found microplastics in all semen and urine samples; each additional polymer type detected was associated with lower sperm count, concentration and progressive motility; PTFE was singled out.

references.authors: Zhang Y, Sun Q, Wang YX, et al.
references.title: Plasticisers chemical mixture, vitamin status, and mortality in US adults: a prospective population-based cohort
references.finding: Each tertile rise in a mixture of eight phthalate metabolites plus BPA was linked to higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.35), but only in people with low vitamin D or red-cell folate; authors attributed about 10% of deaths to the mixture.

references.authors: Zhou Y, Lu Y, Luo Y, et al.
references.title: Associations between concentrations of microplastics in follicular fluid and the risk of diminished ovarian reserve
references.n: 25 women with diminished ovarian reserve, 20 controls
references.finding: Follicular-fluid microplastics (mainly PE, PP, PVC by Py-GC/MS) were higher in diminished ovarian reserve and correlated inversely with AMH and AFC.

references.authors: Zoeller RT, Birnbaum LS, Collins TJ, et al.
references.title: European Medicines Agency Conflicts With the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) on Bisphenol A Regulation
references.finding: Perspective: several agencies including the European Medicines Agency formally disagreed with EFSA's BPA TDI; the authors judge the weight of evidence supports EFSA.

references.authors: Zota AR, Phillips CA, Mitro SD
references.title: Recent Fast Food Consumption and Bisphenol A and Phthalates Exposures among the U.S. Population in NHANES, 2003-2010
references.finding: People getting at least 35% of calories from fast food had 24% higher DEHP and 39% higher DiNP metabolites than non-consumers; no dose-response for BPA.
